HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. Red dawn, low three-quarter from the Goguryeo deck. Foreground left: a dark blurred red banner snapping in the wind. Midground right third: the woman commander of the attached portrait at the bow rail, one boot up on the rail, leaning forward, staring at the wreck; her face and armour exactly the portrait: high topknot with long black hair blowing, grey fur collar, steel lamellar over red cloth. No sword in hand. Background: the burning, heeled-over Silla ship small in the haze, and behind it the red sun breaking the horizon, lighting her face from the front in hard red-gold. Most of the frame is dark sea and smoke. The Silla embassy ship is exactly the attached ship_silla board (broad plain hull, low deck cabin, two masts of cream battened square sails, small blue pennant); the Goguryeo warship is exactly the attached ship_goguryeo board (long high-sided hull, oar gallery, raised stern castle, three cream battened sails, red banners). Same two ships in every frame. Armour is real worn steel lamellar: hundreds of small dull iron plates laced in rows, scuffed and wet, leather and cord showing, weight and dents; never shiny, never toy-like, never cartoon plate. Three planes: a dark out-of-focus foreground shape near the lens, the beat razor-sharp in the midground, the background dissolving into sea haze and smoke; more than half the frame quiet negative space (black sea, dark sky) so the one lit point carries the eye. CHARACTER SHEET, left to right: LEFT face = sooyoung; the 2 tiles after the faces are object references (copy their exact shape); its bottom row is the only sword design. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. YEON SOOYOUNG Colour #b8787a. Any sword is the ancient straight Korean ring-pommel dao: a small iron ring pommel, a short wrapped grip, a thin metal band and NO hand guard, a perfectly straight blade — never a katana, never a tsuba. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
